title: cost-optimization: autotune defaults for batching/caching + quant profiles + unit-econ tooling
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Adds automatic defaults for batching and KV caching, new quantization profile manifests for common model families, and a unit-economics dashboard & CLI export for evaluating per-token cost impact.
description: Motivation: Many customers run into suboptimal per-token unit economics because default batching, KV caching and quant settings are conservative or require manual tuning. This PR introduces a combined set of changes to (1) provide better default autotune settings for batching and KV cache heuristics, (2) add curated quantization profiles that balance latency/quality/cost across common model families, and (3) ship a lightweight unit-economics tool that exports per-route cost breakdowns for experimentation and rollout. Scope: - Runtime heuristics: new default batching window and size heuristics that adapt to request size distribution and customer tier. - KV caching: automatic prefix cache TTL + LRU sizing based on observed prefix hit rates. - Quant profiles: YAML manifests for gpt-like, llama-like and decoder-only variants; new selection logic in the model registry and compatibility checks. - Unit-econ tooling: console dashboard wiring + a CLI csv/json export that computes per-token cost, median/95th latency, and projected monthly spend under traffic patterns. Notes on approach: - Conservative rollout: defaults are opt-in via feature toggle for Private/Dedicated, opt-out for Hosted (we enable gradually per-account via rollout policy). - Tests: end-to-end integration tests added that run small synthetic workloads to validate latency and cache hit gains, plus unit tests for profile parsing and selection. - Observability: new metrics (autotune.batch_window_ms, autotune.estimated_savings_tokens) and a dashboard template included. Checklist: - [x] Runtime heuristics implementation - [x] Quant profiles + model registry wiring - [x] Unit-econ tooling + console wiring - [x] Integration tests - [x] Docs & migration notes - [x] Canaries + rollout policy Changeset summary (high level): - runtime/autotune/strategy.py: implement adaptive batch window and max_batch_size heuristics with backpressure safety. - runtime/cache/kv_autotune.py: add prefix-size estimator, cache TTL heuristics, and instrumentation hooks. - model-registry/quant_profiles/*.yaml: add 6 curated profiles covering fp16/4-bit/8-bit-like variants with expected quality deltas. - tooling/uecon/cli.py: new CLI to export per-route unit econ CSV/JSON. - web/console/routes/unit_econ: dashboard wiring and example queries. - tests/integration/test_autotune_e2e.py: synthetic workloads validating improvements. Migration notes: - No forced changes to existing customers; toggles and accounts rollout are used. - Recommendations for manual overrides included in docs. Impact: In canary runs across 50 internal services we observed median per-token cost reduction of 12-18% with <2% quality regressions (measured by existing eval hooks). CI and validation: initial CI had a flaky integration test (test_cache_eviction) which failed on first run due to timing sensitivity; fixed by adding a deterministic wait hook and re-run. Monitoring & rollback: rollout policy includes automatic fallback to previous defaults if estimated savings drop below 3% or latency SLO degradation >5% for 10m windows. Related: ENG-4532 (autotune initiative), SUP-1284 (customer report highlighting high token costs), ENG-4590 (unit-econ dashboard work)
